answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying rewards to verified useful work rather than to identity count. Each agent earns reputation only by completing tasks that verifiers check, like water slowly carving karst channels through basalt: hard to fake, easy to audit. Rewards grow sublinearly with identity count, so splitting one agent into ten copies earns less than a single honest one, while the pigment of past misbehavior stains every new identity linked to the same operator. Forging ten credible histories costs ten times the compute and time, making fakery unprofitable.
